Diversity-Strength Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch65.R
centrality_dsc.Rd

Diversity-strength centrality (DSC; Zareie et al. 2019) is the product of three properties of the neighbors of a node: how deep they lie in the network on average, how evenly that depth is spread among them, and how much their own neighborhoods differ: $$DSC(v) = \frac{S(v)}{k_v} \; H_1(v) \; JSD(v), \qquad S(v) = \sum_{u \in N(v)} IKs(u).$$ \(IKs\) is the improved k-shell index, \(H_1(v)\) the entropy of the shares \(IKs(u)/S(v)\) and \(JSD(v)\) the Jensen-Shannon divergence of the neighbors' shell distributions, where the shell distribution of \(u\) gives the share of the neighbors of \(u\) in each shell.

Usage

centrality_dsc(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. \(IKs\) is the index centrality_iksd returns. The shells of the divergence term are those of the improved index, as section 3.2 of the source states, although the symbols of its definition name the classic k-shell. The natural logarithm is used; the source prints no base, and another base multiplies every score by one constant. A node with one neighbor scores 0, and so does a node whose neighbors all have the same shell distribution. Isolated nodes score 0. The source prints no node scores; the implementation reproduces the monotonicity values it prints for the rankings built on this score (see centrality_dsr). normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Zareie, A., Sheikhahmadi, A. and Jalili, M. (2019). Influential node ranking in social networks based on neighborhood diversity. Future Generation Computer Systems, 94, 120-129. doi:10.1016/j.future.2018.11.023 .

See also

centrality_dsr, centrality_edsr, centrality_iksd, centrality.

Examples

centrality_dsc(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  1.5840964  1.4279812  2.4262621  0.7725596  0.5203141  1.3470957  0.8604218 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  1.1666690  1.3056283  1.5110591
